Information in the Scores Beyond the Controls

Source: R/spectrum.R
score_spectrum.Rd

Identification in soft_lm() rests on the matrix \(E[a a^\top]\), the covariance of the class probabilities after the controls have been partialled out. score_spectrum() reports its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and the canonical shares: the eigenvalues of \(E[a a^\top]\) relative to the covariance of the scores, that is, for each canonical direction, the fraction of score variance that the controls do not explain.

Usage

score_spectrum(object)

# S3 method for class 'softcats_spectrum'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

Arguments

object

[mandatory] (softcats) A fit returned by soft_lm().

x

[mandatory] (softcats_spectrum) Result of score_spectrum().

digits

[optional] (integer) Number of significant digits to print (default: 3).

...

[optional] Not used.

Value

An object of class softcats_spectrum: a list with values (eigenvalues of \(E[a a^\top]\), decreasing), vectors (eigenvectors, one column per direction), shares (canonical shares, decreasing), min_share, condition (ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue), M and score_cov (covariance of the scores). The print method returns x invisibly.

Details

A share near zero means that, in that direction, the scores are almost a function of the controls and the corresponding contrast is weakly identified. \(E[a a^\top]\) is then nearly singular, and the eigenvector of its smallest eigenvalue shows which categories the weak direction involves.

The shares are estimated from the cross-fitted residuals, which also contain the estimation error of \(E[p \mid X]\). When the controls explain little of the scores, a share can therefore exceed one slightly.

The canonical shares and the following thresholds are conventions of the package. As rules of thumb, a smallest share below 0.05 deserves attention and one below 0.01 means the estimate should not be used. For two categories the single eigenvalue is the residual score variance \(V^*\).

References

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). Coarsening latent-class probabilities: Directional distortion and coverage loss. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.11784

Examples

# Example: Canonical shares with three categories
d <- sim_softcats(n = 2000, K = 3, seed = 4)
fit <- soft_lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = ~ prob_A + prob_B + prob_C,
               data = d, learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 4)
score_spectrum(fit)
#> Score information beyond the controls
#> 
#> Canonical shares not explained by the controls (largest first):
#>     1     2 
#> 0.957 0.861 
#> 
#> Eigenvalues of E[aa'] (eigenvectors dir1, dir2, ...):
#>   dir1   dir2 
#> 0.2120 0.0174 
#> 
#> Condition number: 12.2
#> Weakest direction of E[aa'] (loadings on categories, relative to 'A'):
#>     B     C 
#> 0.720 0.693 
#> 
#> Smallest share 0.861 is adequate.
